newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty criticises Turkey's new detention law.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty criticises Turkey's new detention law.

text.p: Amnesty International criticised Turkey's new detention law on Tuesday, saying it was insufficient and unlikely to prevent torture.

The new law shortens the maximum term of police detention from 30 to 10 days in nine emergency rule provinces and from 14 to seven days in the rest of the country, but the human rights group said it did not go far enough.

"Although we welcome the long-awaited reduction in detention periods, the provisions of this law are insufficient in scope to combat what has become an ingrained system of abuse," Amnesty said in a statement.
"We also regret that our call for an end to incommunicado detention has not been answered," it added.
Parliament passed the law reforming custody procedures last week but it will not come into force until it is signed by President Suleyman Demirel.

Turkey's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minsister Tansu Ciller claimed the new law would comform with European norms on detention periods, but Amensty said neither European nor interntional human rights law endorse four days' incommunicado detention.
Amnesty said it would continue to press for a comprehensive package to tackle torture and to demand that prisoners be given early access to a lawyer.
Earlier on Tuesday, Turkey announced the new law and other proposals which it said would focus on preventing torture in police custory and improve efforts to trace missing people.
The European Parliament has blocked million of dollars of aid to Turkey, partly as a result of its human rights record.
